topic: Understand a codebase you didn't write in one hour: README, run it, follow one feature from the page to the API to the database, read the git log — the skill an internship's first week needs
save_reason: The 1-hour plan for reading any new repo (cheat sheet on slide 7, full steps in the caption), to use on the next open-source project or hackathon repo.
send_reason: Send this to a friend who wants to make their first open-source contribution.

cover.concept: A grand space with one symbolic object: a vast, quiet old library hall with tall wooden shelves, and in the centre aisle one open laptop on a reading table, glowing softly, a brass reading lamp beside it.
hooks: Understand any codebase in one hour. (confidence)
How interns read code they didn't write. (curiosity)
Read a real open-source repo this weekend. (ambition)
You can find your way around any repo. (awe)
cover.hookDraft: Understand any codebase in one hour.
cover.lineDraft: Practise it on one open-source repo this year.

slides.label: Save this
slides.idea: Results first + save promise: a notes file with a one-line map of a repo (where the page, the API and the database live), made in one hour.
slides.title: This is a repo you understand after one hour.
slides.line: Save these 5 steps for the next repo you open.
slides.screen: A Notes file 'repo-map.md' with 3 rows: Page → src/pages/Cart.jsx, API → routes/cart.js, Database → models/Order.js, cropped big

slides.label: Step 1
slides.idea: Read the README and run the project locally before reading any code.
slides.title: Run the project before you read the code.
slides.line: Follow the README setup steps until it opens.
slides.screen: A terminal: npm install, npm run dev, 'Local: http://localhost:3000' highlighted (.focus)

slides.label: Step 2
slides.idea: Break a belief: you don't read every file top to bottom; you look at the folder tree and find the entry points.
slides.title: You don't need to read every file.
slides.line: Look at the folder tree and find where it starts.
slides.screen: VS Code explorer folder tree (src/pages, routes, models, package.json) with src/pages highlighted

slides.label: Step 3
slides.idea: Re-hook: follow one feature (e.g. 'Add to cart') from the page to the API to the database with search.
slides.title: Here's a faster way: follow one button.
slides.line: Search its text and trace it to the database.
slides.screen: VS Code search panel: query 'Add to cart' with 3 results across Cart.jsx, routes/cart.js, models/Order.js

slides.label: Step 4
slides.idea: Won't work unless you write it down: keep a one-line note per file and read the git log for why things changed.
slides.title: This won't work unless you take notes.
slides.line: Write one line about each file you open.
slides.screen: git log --oneline in a terminal with 4 fictional commits, one highlighted

slides.label: Screenshot this
slides.idea: Cheat sheet: 1 Run it (README) · 2 Folder tree · 3 Follow one button · 4 Notes per file · 5 git log for the why.
slides.title: Here's the easy way: screenshot this 1-hour plan.
slides.line: Use it on your next open-source repo.
slides.screen: A Notes note 'New repo in 1 hour' with 5 short rows and minutes per step

slides.idea: Send this to a friend who wants to make their first open-source contribution.
slides.title: Send this to a friend starting open source.
